items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: And there was Slam Stewart, who specialized with the bowed solos. But that was never my thing.

ctx.x: When you first heard him, what did you think?

Well, I said, 'This is the way the bass is supposed to be played.' And I'm sure he inspired all of us. Although prior to that time, I had been playing solos, but nothing like Blanton. He was unbelievable. And there was Slam Stewart, who specialized with the bowed solos. But that was never my thing. My bowing was in the symphony and legitimate type music. I always preferred to play pizzicato solos.
And you say yours weren't anything like his. How would you differentiate what you were playing from what you heard Jimmy Blanton playing?
